process_element_definition: The processes associated with commerce conducted between businesses and final consumers. Customer orders could be fulfilled by direct shipments or customer pick up. B2C order size is generally smaller and has fewer items per order than B2B orders.

process_element_name: Receive B2C Product from Source or Transform
process_element_definition: The activities related to receiving B2C product from Source or Transform, such as receiving product, verifying, recording product receipt, determining put-away location, putting away and recording location that an organization performs at its own warehouses. May include quality inspection.
The process of preparing, verifying, installing, and validating the product at the customer site, if necessary. The product is fully functional upon validation.

process_element_name: Obtain Proof of Delivery or Customer Acceptance
process_element_definition: The activities of sorting and combining products, packing or kitting them, applying labels and bar codes, and delivering the products to the shipping area for loading.

The process of identifying on-hand and scheduled inventory and reserving it for specific orders. It also includes scheduling a delivery date. If a customer is picking up an order, the order availability date can be scheduled instead.

The process of retrieving orders to pick, determining inventory availability, building the pick wave, picking the product, recording the pick, and delivering the products to shipping in response to an order.
The process of sorting and combining products, packing or kitting them, applying labels and bar codes, and delivering the products to the shipping area for loading.

The process of moving packaged products or service resources into a temporary holding or waiting location to await movement to a delivery location. Products made to order may remain in the holding location to await shipment or transfer per the associated customer order.
The process associated with planning product deliveries directly to end customers by coordinating multiple locations, routes, and drivers. It involves both route planning and delivery schedules.
The process associated with keeping customers up to date on their order status and collaborating with the customer to obtain a mutually agreed time and location for product delivery.

process_element_name: Load Vehicle and Generate Shipping Document
process_element_definition: The process of loading products onto modes of transportation and generating the invoice and other documentation required to meet internal, customer, carrier, and government needs. This process may also include verifying the customer’s credit if that has not already been done.
The process of shipping the product, digital or physical, to the customer.

The process associated with commerce between two businesses rather than between a business and an individual consumer. Product is shipped directly to business customers, wholesalers, and retailers. B2B order size are generally larger and has more items per order than B2C.

process_element_name: Receive B2B Product from Source or Transform
process_element_definition: The activities related to receiving B2B product from Source or Transform, such as receiving product, verifying, recording product receipt, determining put-away location, putting away and recording location that an organization performs at its own warehouses. May include quality inspection.
The process of shipping the product, digital or physical, to the customer.
The process of preparing, verifying, installing, and validating the product at the customer site, if necessary. The product is fully functional upon validation.

process_element_name: Obtain Proof of Delivery or Customer Acceptance
process_element_definition: The process of the customer receiving the product and verifying that the order is complete and that the product meets the delivery terms.

The process of identifying on-hand and scheduled inventory reserved for specific orders. It also includes the scheduled delivery date. If a customer is picking up an order, the order availability date instead.

The process of retrieving orders to pick, determining inventory availability, building the pick wave, picking the product, recording the pick, and delivering the products to shipping in response to an order.
The process of sorting and combining products, packing or kitting them, applying labels and bar codes, and delivering the products to the shipping area for loading.

The process of moving packaged products or service resources into a temporary holding or waiting location to await movement to a delivery location. Products made to order may remain in the holding location to await shipment or transfer per the associated customer order.
The process associated with planning product deliveries directly to end customers by coordinating multiple locations, routes, and drivers. It involves both route planning and delivery schedules.
The process associated with keeping customers up to date on their order status and collaborating with the customer to obtain a mutually agreed time and location for product delivery.

process_element_name: Load Vehicle and Generate Shipping Document
process_element_definition: The process of loading products onto modes of transportation and generating the invoice and other documentation required to meet internal, customer, carrier, and government needs. This process may also include verifying the customer's credit if that has not already been done.

The process of sending a signal to the finance department to indicate that the order has been shipped and that the billing process should begin. The order can be closed if payment is received in advance. Otherwise, payment should be received from the customer within the payment terms of the invoice.
The processes associated with fulfilling internal orders delivered to other business units within the same parent organization.

process_element_name: Receive Intra-company Product from Source or Transform
process_element_definition: The activities related to receiving Intra-company product from Source or Transform, such as receiving product, verifying, recording product receipt, determining put-away location, putting away and recording location that an organization performs at its own warehouses. May include quality inspection.
The process of preparing, verifying, installing, and validating the product at the customer site, if necessary. The product is fully functional upon validation.

process_element_name: Obtain Proof of Delivery or Customer Acceptance
process_element_definition: The process of the customer receiving the product and verifying that the order is complete and that the product meets the delivery terms.
The process of sending a signal to the finance department to indicate that the order has been shipped and that the internal financial process should begin.

The process of identifying on-hand and scheduled inventory and reserving it for specific orders. It also includes scheduling a delivery date. If a customer is picking up an order, the order availability date can be scheduled instead.

The process of retrieving orders to pick, determining inventory availability, building the pick wave, picking the product, recording the pick, and delivering the products to shipping in response to an order.
The process of sorting and combining products, packing or kitting them, applying labels and bar codes, and delivering the products to the shipping area for loading.

The process of moving packaged products or service resources into a temporary holding or waiting location to await movement to a delivery location. Products made to order may remain in the holding location to await shipment or transfer per the associated internal order.
The process associated with planning product deliveries to business unit customers by coordinating routes and drivers. It involves both route planning and delivery schedules.

The process associated with keeping business unit customers up to date on their order status and collaborating with the business unit customer to obtain a mutually agreed time and docking location for product delivery.

process_element_name: Load Vehicle and Generate Shipping Document
process_element_definition: The process of loading products onto modes of transportation and generating the financial transaction required to meet internal, carrier, and government needs.
The process of shipping the product, digital or physical, to the business unit.

The process associated with commerce conducted between businesses and final consumers. B2C traditionally referred to mall shopping, eating out at restaurants, pay-per-view movies, and infomercials. However, the rise of the internet created a whole new B2C business channel in the form of e-commerce or selling goods and services through the internet. Online B2C is divided into five categories: direct sellers, online intermediaries, advertising-based B2C, community-based, and fee-based.
The process of gathering, organizing, and analyzing data about your customers; also known as Customer Data Management (CDM).

The process of determining the priority status of a customer. Customer loyalty programs are a crucial mechanism when considering improvements to customer acquisition, satisfaction, and retention rates; visibility of customers and communication strategies; and increased data quality and higher revenue.

The aggregation of the items requested by the customer into an order. Note that requests may come through different channels, and all channels should be monitored, and orders should be processed across multiple channels.

The process of handling credit card authorization captures. Capturing an authorization means the authorized amount of money is transferred from the cardholder account to the merchant account. The capture operation requires a previously successful authorization that has not yet expired. In addition, the payment process includes partial card authorization captures, voids, or refunds.

The process of generating consolidated detailed information from ship notices and their related customer orders, including shipping dates. The information shows that the goods receipts in the account have been sent in response to customer orders. It also shows goods receipt information of each line item's quantities that were ordered, shipped, and invoiced.
The process of collecting, processing cancel requests, and stopping execution.

The process associated with commerce between two businesses rather than between a business and an individual consumer. Transactions at the wholesale level are usually business-to-business, while those at the retail level are most often business-to-consumer (B2C). While business-to-business transactions often involve high prices and volume, they can also happen on a much smaller scale when a small business sells products or services to another small company.
The process of receiving and responding to general customer inquiries and requests for quotes.
The process of entering customer orders in the business's system, identifying on-hand and scheduled inventory, and reserving it for specific orders.

process_element_name: Confirm Inventory Availability and Delivery Date
process_element_definition: The process of identifying the inventory ordered, both on hand and scheduled, and reserving the quantity required for the new order. A delivery date is committed and scheduled.
The process of designating the volume required of on-hand stock to specific orders. Once allocation rules are applied, this stock cannot be used for other orders.
The process of entering and finalizing the customer's order, approving the planned resources, including engineering and manufacturing resources, and officially generating the order.

The process associated with receiving and applying payment from a business customer in accordance with agreed commercial terms. Activities may include generating and issuing invoices, matching payments to purchase orders and goods receipts, applying credits or adjustments, and reconciling accounts. Payment methods can include bank transfers, ACH, checks, or other approved settlement mechanisms. This process also covers handling partial payments, disputed amounts, and issuing refunds or credit memos as required.
The process of transmitting the order through the business's system for fulfillment.
The process of collecting and processing cancel requests and stopping execution on those requests.

The process associated with managing and controlling an internal order through all stages within a business's system. The process tracks which stage an order is in and which stage it should be passed to next. It allows the stakeholders to utilize the system to react to status changes or to replace or add additional functionality.
The process of requesting the movement of stock from one location to another.
The process of reviewing the availability of requested resources to determine a delivery date.
The process of designating the volume required of on-hand stock to specific orders. Once allocation rules are applied, this stock cannot be used for other orders.
The process of confirming that intracompany orders are compliant with established business rules and officially generating the order.
The process of transmitting the order through the business's system for fulfillment.
The process of collecting and processing cancel requests and stopping execution on those requests.

The process of aligning the supply chain strategy to the overall business strategy and ensuring overall optimization of the network, underpinned by sustainable, demand-driven, and customer-focused objectives.

process_element_name: Gather and Analyze Overall Organizational Strategy
process_element_definition: The process associated with determining supply chain strategic goals, performance and sustainability requirements, and implications for supply chain design and operating model from the perspective of the overall organizational strategy. This process answers the question of how the supply chain supports the objectives of the overall strategy.

process_element_name: Communicate Strategic Goals and Initiatives for Implementation
process_element_definition: The process associated with communicating action plans and initiatives to relevant internal stakeholders.

process_element_name: Execute, Monitor, and Measure Strategic Plan with Key Stakeholders
process_element_definition: The process associated with monitoring, measuring, and executing the strategic plan to ensure successful implementation or reassessment.

process_element_name: Define Strategic Supply Chain Context and Scope
process_element_definition: The process associated with determining the 'start' and 'end' of the supply chain strategy vs. other business strategies, e.g., Marketing Strategy, Financial Strategy, and Sales Strategy - All sub-components of the overall organizational strategy.

process_element_name: Gather and Analyze External Supply Chain Insights (Customer, Product, Services)
process_element_definition: The process associated with determining the critical external factors that may impact supply chain strategy success.

process_element_name: Define and Prioritize Product and Service Supply Chain Segments
process_element_definition: The process associated with analyzing the supply chains within an organization to determine the key drivers of supply chain performance and to segment and prioritize those supply chains that have a higher impact on strategic success.

process_element_name: Conduct Strategic Supply Chain Analysis, Benchmarking and Gather Insights (Stakeholders, Competitor, Industry, Markets, etc.)
process_element_definition: The process associated with gathering detailed information on the industry, stakeholders, inter-relationships, and external risks.

process_element_name: Conduct Internal Supply Chain Environment and Strategic Risk Assessment
process_element_definition: The process associated with conducting an internal review of risks and risk responses.

process_element_name: Develop Supply Chain Performance Objectives and Drivers of Strategic Performance Aligned to Strategic Plan
process_element_definition: The process of determining the key drivers of performance that best align with strategic organizational direction.

process_element_name: Review and Validate Supply Chain Operating Model and Organizational Design to Align to Strategic Plan
process_element_definition: The process associated with developing initiatives to improve existing operating model performance.

process_element_name: Coordinate and Align Supply Chain Functional and Process Strategies, Information and Data
process_element_definition: The process associated with connecting internal enablers with initiatives to achieve desired performance in the operating model.

The process of including environmental, social, and governance aspects in business performance decision making. Environmental, Social, and Governance is focused on long-term value creation and is a synonym for sustainability.
The activities required to develop a supply chain strategy that aligns with the overall business sustainability strategy.

process_element_name: Align Plan with Supply Chain Processes, People, Performance, and Practices
process_element_definition: The process in which the desired governance, internal and external, environmental, and social performance is determined for all relevant processes. Furthermore, practices and people's skills are defined and developed to accomplish the desired performance levels.

process_element_name: Develop Materiality Index at the Enterprise Level
process_element_definition: The process of using materiality analysis to develop a materiality index.

process_element_name: Identify and Address Risks Related to the Supply Chain's Economic, Ecological and Ethical Impact
process_element_definition: The process of identifying, collecting, and documenting all potential risk events that may prevent the organization from meeting its goals. This process includes identifying sources of risk.

process_element_name: Strengthen the Supply Chain's Resilience to Disruptions
process_element_definition: The process of developing the capability of a supply chain to anticipate, create plans to avoid or mitigate, and/or to recover from disruptions to supply chain functionality.

process_element_name: Develop Integrated Reporting of the Supply Chain's Economic, Ecological and Ethical Impact
process_element_definition: The process of developing an integrated representation of the company's financial, environmental, and social performance regarding long-term value creation.

The process associated with seamlessly integrating strategic goals, financial objectives, and tactical and operational plans into everyday business decision-making through access to cross-functional data and deliberate alignment. The Enterprise Business Plan is a strategic level plan and is typically reviewed annually, the planning horizon is 3 to 10 years. Changes to the plans in this zone have minimum cost and disruption.

process_element_name: Align Long-Term Financial Plan with Supply Chain Strategy
process_element_definition: The process of aligning the long-term financial plan with the supply chain strategy to achieve their long, medium, and short-term performance goals.

process_element_name: Develop Scenarios to Achieve Business Objectives (Economic, Ecological, Ethical)
process_element_definition: The process of developing scenarios to identify needed responses to meet the economic, environmental, and social objectives of the company along with corporate sustainability goals.

process_element_name: Develop Tactical, Operational, and Supply Chain Plans
process_element_definition: The process that sets operational, tactical, and long-term plans to achieve and sustain the strategic objectives of the business plan that is implemented through the orchestration of resources, actions, and intermediate milestones.

process_element_name: Integrate Tactical, Operational, and Supply Chain Plans with Product Life Cycle Plans
process_element_definition: The process associated with growing, sustaining, and optimizing product life cycle portfolios, including packaging and service, through measures of portfolio health, such as product productivity, supporting launch and phase-out roadmaps, and alignment to commercialization plans, including brand and packaging plans.

process_element_name: Enable Business Decisions to be Made Through Access to Cross-Functional BI Data
process_element_definition: The process of driving decision making through the use of Business Intelligence (BI) software. The iterative Integrated Business Planning process translates decisions into business activities across all stakeholders.

The process of designing and operating distinctly different end-to-end value chains (from customers to suppliers) that are optimized by a combination of unique customer value, product attributes, manufacturing and supply capabilities, and business value considerations.

process_element_name: Define Product and Customer within Supply Chain Definition Matrix
process_element_definition: This process results in a view showing what and where / to whom the organization sells.

process_element_name: Establish Strategy to Meet KPI Targets
process_element_definition: The process of determining the KPI targets based on the strategic requirements for the targeted market segments being monitored.

This process overlays the supply chain related aspects to the product/customer matrix, to determine which characteristics would be relevant to the supply chain design and the degree to which these characteristics impact performance.

This process creates a listing of each intersection of customer / geography and product / product family based on the assigned differentiators (E.g., Forecast ability, customer prioritization, brand priority, supplier types/segments)

This process creates broader segment groupings that are aligned with similar levels of the characteristics already defined, e.g., If two characteristics have been defined, namely ‘Demand Volatility’ and ‘Number of Suppliers’, then, for example, in a set of segments A – G, Segment A, C and D may have a high demand volatility and small supplier base, meaning these may need to be treated in a similar manner when determining the appropriate future operating model.

process_element_name: Competitive Requirements - Determine How Segment Competes
process_element_definition: This process matches the market's competitive requirements with the segment's performance abilities to find the best combination to compete in the marketplace.

process_element_name: Define Operating Model Considerations to Support Competitive Requirements
process_element_definition: The process to define how we run the supply chain operations in a way that aligns with the supply chain strategy to support the market's competitive requirements.
The process to add segment metrics to the balanced scorecard or other benchmarking tools for visibility into segment performance.
The process to deliver the segment metrics for the balanced scorecard.
The process to set the key performance indicators by segment for monitoring.

The process of developing a supply chain that eliminates waste and pollution, circulates products and materials, regenerates nature, and is transitioning to renewable energy and materials. The Circular Supply Chain requires a fundamental shift of thinking for supply chain professionals from the idea of having infinite resources to one where products are reused and repurposed with minimum waste and energy usage. The subprocesses are in order of priority: (1) reduce (2) extend product lifecycle (3) recovery for reuse and repurpose.

process_element_name: Assess the Use of Materials, Water and Energy
process_element_definition: The process of evaluating and quantifying the use of all materials, water, and energy in the end-to-end processes.

process_element_name: Minimize the Use of Materials, Water and Energy
process_element_definition: The process of reducing the use of materials, water, and energy in the end-to-end processes. Lean and Six Sigma processes can jumpstart this reduction, but reexamining materials and transformation processes will be necessary to make substantial reductions.

process_element_name: Increase the Efficient Use of Fixed Assets
process_element_definition: The process of evaluating fixed assets and reducing any inefficiencies or waste in the processes associated with those assets. Inefficiencies waste materials, energy, and employee time. Preventative maintenance, well-trained staff, improving asset utilization ratios, and other techniques can help increase the efficient use of fixed assets. Moreover, the use of energy with the lowest possible environmental impact is prioritized.

The process of evaluating and reducing waste throughout the supply chain. Lean methods can help identify and reduce waste in all areas of the supply chain. Reducing waste can improve productivity, reduce costs, and provide a better working environment.

process_element_name: Extend the Product Life Cycle and Circular Utility
process_element_definition: The process of extending the product lifecycle.

process_element_name: Maximize Recovery for Reuse and Repurpose
process_element_definition: The process to make returns easy and to have an effective procedure for dealing with returns when returns arrive- reuse, repurpose, or dispose of them responsibly. A more effective step is to design sustainability into products and services to maximize the ability to reuse or repurpose returned materials.

The process of establishing, documenting, communicating, and publishing supply chain business rules or policies and assumptions guiding supply chain decisions. A business rule (or policy) is a statement or parameter that defines or constrains some aspect of the business and is generally used in decision-making. Business rules are intended to influence the outcomes of operating the supply chain. They can apply to people, processes, corporate behavior, and computing systems in an organization and are put in place to help the organization achieve its goals while maintaining compliance with internal and external policies and laws. These are often provided as inputs into planning and execution systems.

The process of collecting, organizing, prioritizing, and scheduling policies and directives requiring new supply chain business rules, changes to business rules, or discontinuation of business rules. This process may include scheduling and assigning activities to responsible individuals, groups, or organizations. Several of the business rules that are input into supply chain planning and execution processes may be set and tested during supply chain design.

The process of determining how the policy or directive impacts supply chain processes, technology, and business rules. This process includes reviewing existing business rules and determining the need to add, change or delete business rules.

The process of writing the business rule in the appropriate system of record. This includes adding, editing, and deleting policy and process documentation. A business rule should include a directive or policy, scope, and effective date. Updates to existing business rules may include discontinuation information.

The process of creating awareness in the relevant organization and among the appropriate staff of the upcoming changes. This process may include communication, training, and education programs. For small or incremental changes, a notice may be sufficient. These should ideally be undertaken by a Supply Chain Center of Excellence.

The process of activating the business rule. This process may include the activation of a business rule in a software algorithm and starting to use a new or updated standard operating procedure. This process may include updating external websites and formal notifications to supply chain partners for large-impact business rule changes. This process should include appropriate modeling and testing before full activation in production instances for business rules enacted in software and automated systems. The release of a business rule may be time-phased, such as a bill of materials release for newer revisions.

The process of deactivating a business rule. This process may include archiving the business rule in the associated software to prevent users from inadvertently using it or to comply with regulatory requirements or policies.

The process of defining performance targets for supply chain metrics that align with the overall business strategy and goals. This process also includes reporting performance, identifying performance gaps, performing root cause analyses, and developing and launching corrective actions to close performance gaps. Instituting a continuous improvement program will establish ongoing continuous, incremental improvements. This process describes all levels and versions of managing supply chain performance.

The process of developing a balanced scorecard compares how the supply chain is performing against its defined supply chain strategy. The balanced scorecard uses visualization and is used to measure the effectiveness of an activity against the strategic plans of a company. The balanced scorecard should provide end-to-end supply chain visibility against SCOR attributes (Reliability, Responsiveness, Agility, Cost, Profit, Assets, Environmental, and Social). A Supply Chain Control Tower can help visualize the data collected for the balanced scorecard. External Benchmarking against similar supply chains is recommended to understand how performance compares and how the company is balancing its supply chain performance.

The process of scheduling and running reports and collecting and aggregating performance data. This process includes running standard or predefined reports and ad hoc reporting. Ad hoc reporting includes developing a data collection plan and organizing data collection through inspections, measurements, sampling, and self-assessments.

The process of reviewing the reported performance. This process includes comparing actual performance and trends with the targets set for each metric, identifying metrics that require root cause analysis, notifying process owners, and scheduling the root cause analysis and related resources.
The process of analyzing performance gaps. Performance gaps provide opportunities for improvement.
The process of identifying, documenting, and testing corrective actions to address a root cause to close the related performance gap.
The process of sorting root causes by relative contribution to prioritize them and obtaining approvals, communicating, and launching the corrective actions.

The process of ensuring stated outcomes is continuously measured and managed. This process involves re-occurring leadership reviews to confirm that action plans and set improvement objectives are achieved.

The process of defining and managing the digitalization roadmap for deployment and execution in accordance with the supply chain strategy and available technologies. While progress is made on the agreed technology roadmap, technology review must regularly be conducted to leverage fast-evolving digital solutions.

process_element_name: Define Supply Chain Data, Information and/or Technology Requirements
process_element_definition: The process of synthesizing supply chain capability requirements and technology alternatives into an overarching plan for new technology adoption and alignment to the overall digitalization roadmap.

The process associated with surveying and evaluating available technology options and capabilities. This process can and should occur parallel with "Define supply chain data, information and/or technology requirements" (OE4.1) so that unvetted requirements do not prematurely shape and direct technology or solution research and evaluation.

The process associated with developing a technical blueprint of the arrangement, interaction, and interdependence of all technology components to meet the relevant system requirements. Establish a timeline and focused task group to execute the deployment, including power users and related process stakeholders.

The process associated with the detailed matching of business requirements to the capabilities of technology alternatives to determine the best overall solution, considering fit to requirements, compatibility with other integrating technologies, risks, and total costs of ownership for the technology. Technology selection is a cross-functional activity and is most effective when comprehensive selection criteria and weightings are defined in advance.

process_element_name: Plan and Approve an Implementation Roadmap
process_element_definition: This process starts with creating a project plan for the technology implementation and establishing a timeline and a focused task group, including power users and related process stakeholders, to execute the deployment. The plan coordinates the organizing, planning, scheduling, directing, controlling, monitoring, and evaluating prescribed activities to ensure the achievement of the stated objectives. The next step is to submit the plan to the approval process to validate top management's approval and ensure resource availability (technology, people, finance).

The process associated with developing, configuring, testing, piloting, and fully deploying new supply chain technologies. The technical activities involved in technology deployment are represented in information technology, and engineering implementation best practice approaches and models.

The process associated with continuously improving technology solution performance through ongoing performance analysis and enhancement of the hardware, models, algorithms, data quality captured and/or inputs, and configurations.

The process of verifying that data is accurately captured, and information is properly recorded in the system of record and properly populated to dependent systems. This process includes verifying that information is accessible to users and ensuring a governance process is in place with clearly defined governance rules, gatekeepers, and data owners.

The process of developing, governing, and maintaining an organization of permanent, temporary, and outsourced staff with the right qualifications to support business objectives and supply chain goals. This process includes identifying required and available skills in the organization; determining gaps in skills and competency levels; and identifying training needs, resource gaps, and other resources.

process_element_name: Identify Knowledge, Skill, and Resource Requirements
process_element_definition: The process associated with collecting the required skills to operate part of the supply chain. This process includes planning meetings, periodic performance reviews, and reorganizations. The data collected should list the required skills or resources and is generally organized by an entity such as a supply chain node, department, function, or a combination of these.

process_element_name: Assess Available Knowledge, Skills and Resources
process_element_definition: The process associated with collecting and identifying the skills and resources currently available in the supply chain. Generally, this information is collected and organized by entity, such as supply chain node, department, function, or combination of these. Examples of this process include data collection for standard headcount reports. Headcounts should include temporary staff and outsourced resources.
The process associated with matching skill or resource demands with the available skills or resources.
The process associated with identifying sources of new hires or sources and destinations for redeployment.

The process associated with identifying training and education programs ensures that existing and newly hired employees will have the appropriate skills to perform the work allocated to each employee. An employee, in this definition, includes temporary workers and employees of service providers.

The process associated with obtaining approvals for hiring, redeployment, training, and education plans, prioritizing these plans and executing them. Additional resources and skill requirements will create the need to adjust the labor component of capacity in the Orchestrate Supply Chain, Plan, Order, Source, Transform, Fulfill, and Return processes over time.

process_element_name: Monitor Performance of Skills Development Program and ROE (Return on Education)
process_element_definition: The process associated with monitoring employee performance, changes in required skills, development programs, and the financial return on education (ROE).

The process of managing and communicating contractual and non-contractual agreements. These agreements support business objectives and supply chain goals. This process includes all agreements related to supply chain operations, including material and services acquisition, inventory-stocking practices and levels, performance targets, planning and decision-making, logistics and delivery, and data exchange and visibility.

This process associated with creating a contract or Service Level Agreement (SLA). A contract must include information such as effective date and duration, customer or supplier address, and payment terms; it must not conflict with business rules or regulatory requirements, and it must have clearly defined service level criteria and remedial actions as part of the contract.

The process associated with receiving new contracts or changes to existing contracts. These contract updates may originate in the sales and support department if they are for customer contracts or in the product and process design department if they are for contracts with material or service providers. This process includes the validation of contracts against criteria and business rules.

The process associated with entering contractual information into document management systems, such as a Contract Lifecycle Management system) and enterprise resources planning systems. This process includes translating contractual language and information into a format the systems can comprehend. A final step in this process is distributing the contract or updates to an existing contract to the appropriate processes and functions.

The process associated with activating or deactivating and archiving a contract. This process may include updating information statuses in document management systems or enterprise resources planning (ERP) systems. This activity may be triggered by the document management system, or the ERP system based on parameters entered as part of the Record and Distribute (OE6.2) process.

The process associated with reviewing contractual parties' performance, including suppliers and customers. This process includes comparing the contractual service-level agreements with the actual service levels. It may be triggered by a calendar event, such as annual or quarterly quality reviews, or actual performance issues identified in daily supply chain processes.

The process associated with identifying and prioritizing key performance issues or areas of ongoing process improvement. This process includes notifying contractual partners of non-conformance to contractual agreements or service-level agreements. It also addresses non-compliance or severe issues and areas of continuous improvement, which tend to be less severe and support common interests.
The process associated with identifying ways to address non-compliance or how to implement performance improvements.

The process associated with selecting, obtaining approvals for, and prioritizing the appropriate issue resolutions and then distributing the selected resolution(s) to the appropriate processes or functions.
The activities associated with ending the contractual relationship. Terminations could be due to completion or an impossibility of performance, mutual agreement, breach of contract, or rescission.

The process of defining and managing the geographic and activity footprint of a supply chain. This process defines the location of facilities and assigns resources, distribution networks, suppliers, customers, materials, products, capacities, and capabilities to those locations.

The process associated with initiating a supply chain optimization project. This process begins with determining what part of the supply chain network to assess; this sets the project's scope. Organizations that manage the supply chain network as a project structure must establish a project organization. Organization selection includes identifying and securing the availability of a sponsor, stakeholders, and data or information providers and selecting project team members.
The process associated with identifying the objective of the supply chain and collecting the data required to describe or model the supply chain at the level necessary.

The process associated with developing what-if scenarios to support different strategies and projections. Scenarios may be developed for different detailed strategies, requirements, and potential internal or external changes. Activities include management interviews and external transportation and warehousing studies. Initial review of developed scenarios may result in rejection of the scenario or the decision to proceed to simulation.

The process associated with developing models or simulation models to run what-if scenarios through a validation process. Simulation models may use automation, but conference room pilots or walk-throughs may also serve this purpose. The simulation's objective is to validate each scenario's feasibility and find possible network or process design flaws. Automated simulation tools may also predict the performance of the new network or processes by simulating the processing of large numbers of orders.

The process associated with estimating the effort, risks, and results of implementing a scenario. Activities include estimating risks, funding duration, and the staff and skills required to implement the scenario. Risks include estimates of the impact on the value at risk for the supply chain. Results include changes that need to be made to the performance of the supply chain for all relevant metrics.

The process associated with recommending and obtaining approvals for proposed supply chain network or configuration changes. This process includes reviewing the what-if scenarios and their impact or benefit results with key stakeholders. The objective of this process is to identify the optimal solution and present this recommendation to the sponsor and stakeholders and obtain approval to develop the change program.

The process associated with developing the roadmap for the change program. This process includes identifying the steps or projects required to implement facility changes, contracted parties, staffing, automation, and processes.

process_element_name: Propose Resource Plan and Gain Budget Approval (Including Change Management)
process_element_definition: The process associated with following the approval steps needed for securing the budget and resources required for the project. In addition, during this process, develop the training programs and enablement materials required for change management.

process_element_name: Kick Off Project and Monitor Progress
process_element_definition: The process associated with coordinating, starting, and monitoring the individual change projects. This process includes supporting the establishment of change projects, coordinating launch dates, and communicating reporting requirements. Steps also may include archiving the supply chain network or configuration project documentation for future reference and dissolving the project team. Dissolving the project team requires transferring the monitoring responsibility to the appropriate organizations.

The process of identifying, collecting, and assessing regulatory compliance requirements and integrating them into standard supply chain processes, policies, and business rules. This process also includes managing voluntary compliance with standards and certifications.

process_element_name: Determine Regulatory and Compliance Requirements that Apply to Business and Future Compliance Requirements
process_element_definition: The process of identifying, collecting, and assessing relevant regulatory compliance requirements and forecasting and predicting future regulatory changes affecting supply chain processes, including changes to standards, certifications, and the creation of new regulatory bodies.
The process associated with identifying regulatory bodies, subscribing to their publications, and receiving and reviewing them.

The process associated with reading, interpreting, and researching policies, laws, rules, and regulations. This process includes determining if and how these regulatory requirements apply to a supply chain.

process_element_name: Identify Deficiencies / Gaps vs the New / Projected Regulations
process_element_definition: The process associated with identifying current and future regulatory requirements that are not being met or cannot be met using existing processes, business rules, and policies. This process includes notifying impacted organizations about the deficiency status.
The process associated with identifying remediation alternatives, selecting and documenting processes, policies, and business rules, and setting documentation requirements to remediate a deficiency.

process_element_name: Verify that Remediation Steps Have Been Effective
process_element_definition: The process associated with verifying the remediation strategy with controlling entities and obtaining a license certifying compliance with the controlling entity’s laws, rules, or regulations.

The process associated with approving and implementing changes to processes, policies, and business rules. This process may include distributing certification documentation to relevant organizations in the supply chain.
The process of identifying and assessing potential disruptions and risks in the supply chain and developing a plan to mitigate these threats.

The process of defining and documenting the objectives and internal and external scope for managing risk. This process includes developing and maintaining an understanding of the internal and external relationships and the internal and external factors that influence the supply chain's ability to achieve its objectives and defining and maintaining a risk management organization made of stakeholders, a governance structure, procedures, and a schedule.
The process of identifying, collecting, and documenting all potential risk events, and their sources, which may prevent the organization from meeting its goals.

The process of collecting and documenting for each potential risk the causes, probability of occurrence, and consequences. The standard metric for quantification of risk is value at risk (VaR): VaR = Probability of Occurrence x Monetary Impact of Occurrence.
The process of prioritizing risk events by value at risk and determining for each risk whether mitigation actions are required or if the risk is acceptable.

The process of determining the actions required to eliminate, reduce, or accept and monitor a risk. This process can include creating, approving, communicating, and launching the risk mitigation plan.
The process associated with approving and implementing a risk resolution strategy. This process includes actions to mitigate, avoid or accept risk.

The process of developing and establishing courses of action that represent a projected appropriation of supply chain resources to meet supply chain requirements. This is done at the operational level of planning and is typically reviewed monthly.
The process of collecting and analyzing external factors that may influence the demand requirements.

The process of identifying, aggregating and prioritizing all sources of demand for the integrated supply chain of a product or service at the appropriate level, horizon and interval. The sales forecast is composed of the following concepts: sales forecasting level, time horizon and time interval. The sales forecasting level is the level of detail required for the forecast, such as the corporate level, division level, product line level, stock keeping unit level, or stock keeping unit by location level. The sales forecasting time horizon generally coincides with the time frame of the plan for which it was developed, such as an annual, monthly, weekly or daily timeline. The sales forecasting time interval generally coincides with how often the plan is, such as a daily, weekly, monthly or quarterly time frame.

The process of collecting and analyzing internal and external supply requirements to meet the unconstrained demand/requirements. This process will include the capacity, capability, and availability of products and resources needed to meet the demand over the planning horizon.

process_element_name: Balance External Market Signals, Supply Chain Requirements, and Supply Chain Response Using Supply Chain Modeling Techniques
process_element_definition: The process of identifying and measuring the gaps and imbalances between demand and resources to determine how to best resolve the variances through marketing, pricing, packaging, warehousing, outsourcing plans, or some other action that will optimize service, flexibility, costs, assets, or other supply chain inconsistencies in an iterative and collaborative environment. Includes developing a time-phased course of action that commits supply chain resources to meet supply chain requirements.

process_element_name: Replan, Analyze, and Select Optimal Supply Chain Response
process_element_definition: The process of realigning the supply and demand plans, as required, to meet the business and supply chain goals.

process_element_name: Communicate Plan to Execution Functions and Evaluate
process_element_definition: The process of establishing and communicating courses of action, throughout the appropriate time-defined planning horizon and interval, which represent a projected appropriation of supply chain resources to meet supply chain requirements.
The process of developing and establishing courses of action that represent a projected appropriation to meet order requirements as part of the order management processes.
The process of identifying, aggregating, and prioritizing all sources that would generate an order in the integrated supply chain of a product or service.

process_element_name: Assess and Create Initial Order Processing Response
process_element_definition: The process of collecting and analyzing internal and external order processing requirements to meet the unconstrained demand/requirements. This process will include the capacity, capability, and availability of resources needed to satisfy the processing orders over the planning horizon.

The process of identifying and measuring the gaps and imbalances between order demands and the resources to support them to determine how to best resolve the variances with some action that will optimize service, flexibility, and other supply chain inconsistencies in an iterative and collaborative environment.

process_element_name: Replan, Analyze, and Select Optimal Order Response
process_element_definition: The process of realigning the order management processing plan and the demand plan, as required, to meet the business and supply chain goals by altering, as required, the order processing or resource plan.

process_element_name: Communicate Finalized Order Response Back to P1.3
process_element_definition: The process of establishing and communicating courses of action, throughout the appropriate time-defined planning horizon and interval, which represent a projected appropriation of supply chain resources to meet supply chain requirements for the order management process.

The process of developing and establishing courses of action throughout specified time periods that represent a projected appropriation of material resources to meet supply chain requirements' sourcing activities.
The process of identifying, prioritizing, and considering as a whole, and the constituent parts, all sources of demand for a product or service in the supply chain.

process_element_name: Assess and Create Initial Source Response
process_element_definition: The process of establishing courses of action, throughout specified time periods, which represent a projected appropriation of supply resources needed to meet sourcing plan requirements.
The process of developing a time-phased review and course of action scenarios that balance and commits sourcing supply resources to fulfill customer order requirements.

process_element_name: Replan, Analyze, and Select Optimal Source Response
process_element_definition: The process of realigning the sourcing plan and the demand plan to meet the business and supply chain goals by altering, as required, the sourcing activities, demand plan, and resource plan.

process_element_name: Communicate Finalized Source Response Back to P1.3
process_element_definition: The process of developing and establishing courses of action throughout specified time periods that represents a projected appropriation of source resources to meet the source requirements.

The process of developing and establishing courses of action throughout specified time periods that represents a projected appropriation of production resources to meet the transformation (e.g., production or service) requirements.
The process of identifying, prioritizing, and considering as a whole, with constituent parts, all sources of demand in creating a product or service.

process_element_name: Assess and Create Initial Transform Response
process_element_definition: The process of establishing courses of action, throughout specified time periods, which represent a projected appropriation of supply resources to meet production and operating plan requirements.
The process of developing a time-phased review and course of action scenarios that balance operation resources to fulfill operation requirements.

process_element_name: Replan, Analyze, and Select Optimal Transform Response
process_element_definition: The process of realigning the production plan and the demand plan to meet the business and supply chain goals by altering, as required, the demand plan or transformation activities to support the business requirements.

process_element_name: Communicate Finalized Transform Response back to P1.3
process_element_definition: The process of establishing and communicating courses of action, throughout the appropriate time-defined planning horizon and interval, which represent a projected appropriation of supply chain resources to meet supply chain requirements for the transformation process.
The process of developing and establishing courses of action throughout specified time periods that represent a projected appropriation of delivery resources to meet fulfillment requirements.
The process of identifying, prioritizing, and considering as a whole, with constituent parts, all sources of demand in fulfilling a product or service.

process_element_name: Assess and Create Initial Fulfillment Response
process_element_definition: The process of identifying, evaluating, and considering as a whole, with constituent parts, all things that add value to the fulfillment of a product or service.
The process of developing a time-phased course of action that commits delivery resources to meet delivery requirements.

process_element_name: Replan, Analyze, and Select Optimal Fulfillment Response
process_element_definition: The process of aligning the fulfillment process plan and the demand plan to meet the business and supply chain goals by altering, as required, the demand or fulfillment activities to support the business requirements.

process_element_name: Communicate Finalized Fulfillment Response Back to P1.3
process_element_definition: The process of establishing and communicating courses of action, throughout the appropriate time-defined planning horizon and interval, which represent a projected appropriation of supply chain resources to meet supply chain requirements for the fulfillment process.

The strategic or tactical process of establishing and adjusting courses of action or tasks throughout specified time periods that represent a projected appropriation of return resources and assets to meet anticipated and unanticipated return requirements. The scope includes unplanned returns of sold merchandise and planned returns of rotable products. The process includes developing and establishing refurbished products for reissue to customers.
The process of identifying, evaluating, and considering as a whole, with constituent parts, all sources of demand for the return of a product.

process_element_name: Assess and Create Initial Return Response
process_element_definition: The process of establishing courses of action throughout specified time periods that represent a projected appropriation of required return resources or assets to meet return process requirements.
The process of developing plans that make it possible to commit return resources or assets to satisfy return requirements.

process_element_name: Replan, Analyze, and Select Optimal Return Response
process_element_definition: The process of aligning the return process plan and the demand plan to meet the business and supply chain goals by altering, as required, the demand or return activities to support the business requirements.

process_element_name: Communicate Finalized Return Response Back to P1.3
process_element_definition: The process of establishing and communicating courses of action throughout specified time periods that represent a projected appropriation of required return resources or assets to meet return process requirements.

The process associated with the receipt, diagnosis, dispositioning, and positioning of returned products. Return activity includes decision-making associated with circular considerations, optimization of the return pathway, including across country borders, entitlement verifications, and inventory management considerations.

process_element_name: Initiate, Authorize, Schedule, Verify Product Return
process_element_definition: The process is associated with a product return by an individual, organization, or third party. The return begins with an acceptance or rejection based on the Service Agreement Terms and Conditions. If the product is accepted, the product is authorized for return, and the product return is scheduled or accepted.
The process of gathering internal B2B product receipt data and distributing it among the required parties.

The process associated with receiving a returned product by the OEM, OEM partner, last known holder, designated return center, or other service provider, such as an approved field engineer. A check is performed to compare product condition to any approved return authorization. The entity receiving the return may immediately initiate a rapid adjustment and either return the product to the customer or begin product return internally. The item is prepared for transfer/shipment if required.

process_element_name: RMA Close or Adjust Return Order
process_element_definition: The process where the OEM, OEM partner, last known holder, designated return center, or other service provider, such as an approved field engineer, formally confirms receipt of the return product and closes the RMA order or formally adjusts the RMA/return order, notifying the required parties of details and acting on the updated closure/adjustment.

The process associated with the testing and/or diagnosis of the returned product. Product condition is compared to the expected condition based on Customer input, remote sensing, or other reports. The original labeling of condition is confirmed, adjusted, or the product is sent for further testing/diagnosis.

The process associated with the decision process by which the Return Product is channeled for immediate replacement into stock, refurbishment, recertification, upgrade, remanufacturing, reuse, repair, repurposing, recycling, disassembly with component dispositioning, reclamation, disposal, or another activity. Serial number tracing may be required.
The process associated with requesting additional/updated documentation for the movement of the Returned Product. The request may include new tests, analysis, and regulatory documentation.

The process associated with the signaling and physical movement of the product to the next location or storage, as per the dispositioning process. This process includes updating the database(s) with the product status and location, the condition of the product, and a notation of the change of ownership.

The process associated with the adjustment of Financial Terms including issuing reimbursements, receipt of payment, and financial change(s) to terms and conditions. This process also includes adjusting the Contract/Service Agreement terms and conditions, including an allowance for an upgrade at the time of the return, waiving of requirements at the time of return, and the inclusion of temporary or permanent changes.

The process associated with short-term or long-term storage for the returned product, also called On-Hold Inventory. Storage must meet regulatory requirements for security (cyber and physical), product tracking, environmental, and health protections.

The process associated with the receipt, diagnosis, and activity required of Returned Services. Service Return may be handled digitally, face-to-face, such as formal meetings or requests, or via other communication pathways. Financial, entitlement, environmental, and other considerations are included.

The process associated with a Return Service request/requirement that is initiated via:
- OEM/Company/Government/Other initiation.
- Service update/upgrade/replacement based on Service Agreement Terms and Conditions.
- Customer request due to non-conformance.
- Adjustment required due to inability for further activity or use of service.

The process associated with a formal acknowledgment of the return of service and any associated change items requested by the customer and approved for action by the OEM, OEM partner, last known holder, designated service center, or other approved service provider. In some cases, the entity receiving the return may initiate a rapid adjustment/solution and reinstate the service immediately.

The process associated with the receipt of Customer signoff/approval by the OEM, an OEM partner, last known holder, designated service center, or other approved service provider. The customer signoff means that the service requested has been received and worked on, and the fix is working as per specification. In some cases, the customer request is outside acceptable specification/contract/other limits and is adjusted based on additional conversation with the customer, or the service request may be canceled, a reason code sent, and the Service Change Order closed. Otherwise, closure is caused by the return of the product to the customer or a receipt of replacement from the customer.

The process by which the Service Change is tested and/or diagnosed against the previously agreed service requirements and specifications. Original description/labeling of the condition is confirmed, adjusted, or sent for further testing/diagnosis.

The process associated with the adjustment of financial terms, including issuing of reimbursements, receipt of payment, and adjustment to the financial terms and conditions included in the contract or service agreement.

The process associated with additional/updated documentation required for the Returned Service. The process may include design adjustment requirements, change requests, and aspects leading to non-compliance.

The process associated with the signaling and movement of a Service Request to the next party in the service chain such as software design, configuration, service center support, partner support, and/or senior management.

The process associated with the Maintenance, Repair, and Overhaul process set differentiates itself by returning the same product unit to the Return originating Customer, as verified by product Serial Number or other Unit ID means. In some instances, as per the Service Agreement or Contract, the replacement item may be a previously stocked repaired item. The Return MRO processes do not represent the actual maintenance, repair, or overhaul activities; these are generally represented by Transform processes.

The process by which the OEM/company/government initiates a recall of the product. The OEM/company begins an update/upgrade/replacement based on the Service Agreement Terms and Conditions. The product is authorized for return due to the occurrence or anticipation of the risk of product failure/non-compliance; the entitlement to return is verified; the product return is scheduled. The product serial number is recorded and traced. Accepting the request may include negotiating the conditions of the return with the customer and authorizing a return replacement or credit. Rejecting the request would include providing the customer with a reason for the rejection.

The process associated with receiving a returned MRO product by the OEM, OEM partner, last known holder, designated return/service center/depot, or approved entity. The unit serial number/unit ID and condition is verified against the return authorization and required documentation. If possible, the receiving entity or onsite field engineer will fix/adjust the product and immediately return the product to the customer. The item is prepared for transfer/shipment if required.

The process associated with providing a quote to the customer by the OEM, OEM partner, last known holder, designated return/service center/depot, or approved entity, either remotely or onsite, for the anticipated MRO service due to out-of-warranty/service agreement condition. The unit cannot continue in the MRO process until the customer verifies the quote and approves the associated payment and other terms.

The process associated with the testing and/or diagnosis of the returned MRO unit. Product condition is compared to the expected condition based on Customer input, remote sensing, or other reports. Original labeling of the condition is confirmed, adjusted, or sent for further testing/diagnosis.

The process associated with the decision process by which the diagnosis/MRO testing results, country of ownership, and other attributes are used to initiate inventory requirements for required repair(s), confirm capacity at the location or applicable locations, compare the cost of unit's movement into and out of acceptable and allowed locations, and schedule within required time limits.
The process associated with creating or updating the documentation required for Returned MRO product movement, status capture, and regulatory requirements.

The process associated with the signaling and physical movement of the product to the next location, or storage, as per the dispositioning process. This process includes updating the database(s) with the product status and location, the condition of the product, and a notation of the change of ownership.

The process associated with the adjustment of Financial Terms including issuing reimbursements, receipt of payment, and financial change(s) to terms and conditions. This process also includes adjusting the Contract/Service Agreement terms and conditions, including an allowance for an upgrade at the time of the return, waiving of requirements at the time of return, and the inclusion of temporary or permanent changes or adjustments based on country legal requirements.

The process associated with temporary storage for returned product. Storage must meet regulatory requirements for security (cyber and physical), product tracking, environmental and health protections, and country legal requirements for product movement and timing.

The process associated with locating and sourcing key suppliers, which often includes analyzing total spend. This process focuses on developing long-term relationships with trading partners who can help the purchaser meet profitability and customer satisfaction goals. Information technology applications include E-Procurement, automation of request for quote (RFQ), request for proposal (RFP), electronic auctioning (e-auction or reverse auction), and contract management systems.

The process associated with defining and understanding the business opportunity or need. This process involves cross-functional stakeholder involvement to develop a comprehensive high-level specification. Whether for performance or conformance, a specification is a systematic statement of the requirements to be satisfied in the supply of a product or service and sits at the heart of the contract between the buyer and the seller. Developing a specification must define the business requirements clearly and communicate these to suppliers effectively to facilitate the evaluation of goods and services against the agreed specification.

The process associated with post-tender negotiation. Whole-life costs should also be considered, including decommissioning, removal, or disposal costs. After negotiation, developing a contract will allow both the customer and the chosen supplier to fully understand the agreement's obligations and key success criteria. The agreed terms and conditions help minimize contractual risks and exposure when doing business. Once the contract and terms are agreed upon, the communication and implementation process can begin. Clear timelines and parameters should be set up on both sides. Both parties should also form relevant stakeholder groups to effectively manage the contract implementation.

This process is associated with conducting a supply market opportunity analysis to assess available supply market options. This analysis helps identify the potential suppliers and the degree of competition in the supply market. It also entails conducting make or buy analysis.

The process of developing a sourcing strategy or plan to procure the products and services required by the organization. Inputs into this process include specifications, business requirements, and marketplace assessments. The sourcing strategy or plan must adhere to external laws and regulations and internal policies and guidelines. The plan must account for supply chain risks and consider options like conducting a competitive tender, developing the product in-house, using a sole supplier or single source of supply, dual sourcing, in-country value, and centralized vs. decentralized procurement.

The activities associated with testing the market to determine if it is the right time to release a product or service into the marketplace. This process might uncover other factors to consider, including what competitors are doing, supplier performance, and new legislation.

The process of screening the market to identify an organization that provides a needed good or service. Given a set of criteria, the sourcing team will use different methodologies to identify potential suppliers that meet their criteria.

The process of prequalifying suppliers. This process assesses a potential supplier's capability to control factors such as quality, delivery, quantity, price, financial stability, and all other factors to be embodied in a contract. The importance of supplier prequalification is that it is an essential aspect of both strategic sourcing, supplier management, and the achievement of competitive advantage.

The process of determining the intensity of supplier collaboration driven by the sourcing strategy, category management, and material/services classification, which would result in the decision to form virtual alliances, strategic alliance, partnering, ongoing relationship, or even arm's length collaboration.

The process of sending a formal invite to tender (ITT) and/or a request for quote (RFQ) to selected potential suppliers. Items included are project specifications, documentation about the business requirements, and clear timelines for response.

The process of evaluating and validating bids and proposals to select the preferred supplier(s). Tender evaluation should be carried out in a structured, disciplined, and transparent manner, regardless of whether the contracts are for the supply of goods or services. Most evaluations explore price comparisons alongside technical capabilities, capacity, quality of service, and the supplier's financial health.

The process associated with the procurement of products or services that forms the final product, such as raw materials used in the transformation process to make finished products and services sold to consumers.

The process associated with determining the approach that will trigger orders to the supplier. Depending on factors like sourcing strategy and collaboration arrangement, this can take many forms, such as PO, Kanban, MRP, supplier-triggered replenishment, prearranged delivery schedules, or a delivery request from a call-off. This process is part of short-term planning and is typically within the Frozen Time Fence and changes cannot be made without senior management approval. It is managed daily with a planning horizon of 1 to 30 days.

The process of scheduling and managing the execution of individual product deliveries in the context of existing contracts or purchase orders. The requirements for product releases are determined based on a detailed sourcing plan or other types of product pull signals.

The process of moving materials from suppliers or vendors into customer storage facilities. This process is part of the inbound logistics order management process. Inbound order management entails various activities, including planning, directing, monitoring, and controlling the processes related to purchase orders, such as outsourcing logistics service providers, coordinating documentation, tracking, and tracing shipments.

The process and activities of receiving products to contract requirements. By planning the receiving operation, logistics professionals can schedule inbound shipments so that they can be quickly unloaded and moved from the receiving area into the storage location. This process is facilitated by coordinating shipment arrivals with labor availability and preparing crews for a shipment’s anticipated unloading needs (e.g., special equipment).

The process and activities required to determine a product or service's conformance to specifications and the statement of work. It entails sampling, verifying marks, and testing to accept or reject products and services.

The process of transferring accepted products to the appropriate stocking location within the organization. This process includes all the activities associated with repackaging, staging, moving, and stocking products. For services, this is the transfer or application of a service to the final customer or end user.
The process of authorizing payments and paying suppliers for products or services. This process includes invoice collection, invoice matching with receiving, and the issuance of payment.

The process associated with procuring the goods and services the organization needs to continue operating but are not directly linked to producing the products and services it sells. Although important to an organization, some indirect procurement can be sourced from several different suppliers, and as a result, supplier relationships can differ from those in direct procurement. A few examples of indirect procurement include rent, utilities, MRO supplies, capital expenditures, and services.

The process associated with determining the approach that will trigger orders to the supplier. Depending on factors like sourcing strategy and collaboration arrangement, this can take many forms, such as PO, Kanban, MRP, supplier-triggered replenishment, prearranged delivery schedules, or a delivery request from a call-off. This process is part of short-term planning and is typically within the Frozen Time Fence and changes cannot be made without senior management approval. It is managed daily with a planning horizon of 1 to 30 days.

The process of scheduling and managing the execution of individual product deliveries in the context of existing contracts or purchase orders. The requirements for product releases are determined based on a detailed sourcing plan or other types of product pull signals.

The process of moving materials from suppliers or vendors into customer storage facilities. This process is part of the inbound logistics order management process. Inbound order management entails various activities, including planning, directing, monitoring, and controlling the processes related to purchase orders, such as outsourcing logistics service providers, coordinating documentation, tracking, and tracing shipments.

The process and activities of receiving products to contract requirements. By planning the receiving operation, logistics professionals can schedule inbound shipments so that they can be quickly unloaded and moved from the receiving area into the storage location. This process is facilitated by coordinating shipment arrivals with labor availability and preparing crews for a shipment’s anticipated unloading needs (e.g., special equipment).

The process and activities required to determine a product or service's conformance to specifications and the statement of work. It entails sampling, verifying marks, and testing to accept or reject products and services.

The process of transferring accepted products to the appropriate stocking location within the organization. This process includes all the activities associated with repackaging, staging, moving, and stocking products. For services, this is the transfer or application of a service to the final customer or end user.
The process of authorizing payments and paying suppliers for products or services. This process includes invoice collection, invoice matching with receiving, and the issuance of payment.
The process associated with the return and disposition decisions for business reasons, agreements, or arrangements such as defective, excess, or for maintaining or repairing.

The process of initiating a source return. Upon notification of a non-conformity resulting from inspection or another source, such as near expiry product, defect in the product, or malfunction. The organization initiates the return of the product(s) to the next entity in the upstream supply network.

The process of requesting and obtaining authorization to return a product to a supplier or service provider. In addition, the customer must receive information such as return replacement or credit, packaging, handling, transportation, and import and export requirements to facilitate the efficient return of the product.

The process of assigning a reason for the return of the product, such as the degree, class, and nature of the defect. Other return reasons include a return for repair, excess stock, expired replacement, recall, Third-Party Disposal, salvage, Third-Party Sale (secondary markets), rework, remanufacture/refurbish, modify, repair, Return to Vendor, resale, scrap/destroy.

The process of developing the logistics of the return, such as scheduling for a carrier to pick up the defective product for delivery to the supplier. The logistics activities may depend on the contractual agreements between the supplier and the organization.
