The process of closing or adjusting the return order upon completion of the return process. In addition, the return order status is changed to Complete. This process can be manual or automated.

The process of transforming raw materials, ingredients, components, or sub-assemblies to create a tangible product through labor, machinery, tools, and biological or chemical processing or formulation.

The process associated with the engineering or configuration activities required after an order's acceptance but before the product or deliverable can be produced. This process may include generating and delivering final drawings, specifications, formulas, or part programs. In general, this is the last step in completing any preliminary engineering work done as part of the quotation process.

The process of scheduling and managing the execution of the activities required to create a product. Scheduling is typically done according to plans to produce specific parts, or product formulations, in specified quantities and the planned availability of required sourced products. This process includes sequencing and, depending on the factory layout, any standards for setup and run. Intermediate production or value-adding activities are generally coordinated before scheduling the operations needed to create a finished product.

The process associated with the selection and physical movement of sourced or in-process products, including raw materials, fabricated components, subassemblies, required ingredients, and intermediate formulations or services, from a stocking or resource location to a specific point-of-use location. Issuing a product or resource includes the corresponding system transactions. The bill of materials or bill of service, routing information, and recipe or production instructions will determine the products to be issued to support the production operation(s).
The series of activities performed on sourced and in-process products to convert them from a raw or semi-finished state to a state of completion and greater value.

The activities associated with inspection. These activities include examination and testing. Examination can be visual or dimensional, relying on the human senses or using simple methods of measurement and handling. Testing includes techniques by which functional, measurable characteristics, operability, supportability, or performance capability are quantitatively verified when subjected to controlled conditions that are real or simulated. Inspection is generally non-destructive and typically includes sight, hearing, smell, touch, taste, simple physical manipulation, mechanical and electrical gauging, and measurement. Testing often uses special test equipment or instrumentation to obtain accurate quantitative data to be analyzed.

The activities that containerize completed products for storage or sale to end users. Within certain industries, package activities may include cleaning or sterilization. Package activities do not apply to services.

The activities associated with the post-production documentation, testing, or certification required before delivering a finished product to the end customer. Examples include the assembly of batch records for regulatory agencies, laboratory tests for potency or purity, the creation of certificates of analysis or other quality records, and sign-off by the quality organization.

process_element_name: Disposition Waste or Surplus (Scrap, Recycle, Repurpose)
process_element_definition: The activities associated with collecting and managing waste or surplus produced during the value-add and testing processes. Waste or surplus can include scrap material, unused resources, and non-conforming products or deliverables.

The process of scheduling, maintaining and dispositioning of product transformation assets developed for supply chain execution. This includes installation, calibration and other activities necessary to sustain supply chain execution.
The processes associated with delivering value to customers by facilitating outcomes customers want to achieve, but without the ownership of specific costs and risks.

The activities associated with determining the optimal location, layout for effective customer flow and work flow, procedures and job definitions for service providers, measures to ensure quality, the extent of customer involvement, equipment selection, and adequate service capacity.
The activities associated with requesting customer payment for the services rendered and providing acknowledgment to the customer stating that the payment has been received.
The activities associated with ending the contractual relationship. Terminations could be due to completion or an impossibility of performance, mutual agreement, breach of contract, or rescission.
The activities associated with regaining possession of the resources and service components commissioned during the service provision.

The activities associated with collecting and managing waste or surplus produced during all stages of the service life cycle - introduction, growth, maturity, and decline. Waste or surplus can include scrap material, unused resources, and non-conforming products or deliverables.

process_element_name: Determine the Scope of Service Order and Associated SLAs
process_element_definition: The activities associated with outlining the services that need to be performed by the service provider, including the customer expectations related to the quality of work, volume of work, precision, accuracy, responsiveness, speed, and efficiency.
The process associated with determining and managing the service system capacity and utilization by better matching the supply of and demand for service.

The activities associated with collecting and identifying the skills and resources currently available in the supply chain. Generally, this information is collected and organized by entity, such as supply chain node, department, function, or a combination of these. Examples of this process include data collection for various service components, including servers, serving stations, and queues.

The activities associated with initiating a service action based on a request from a user, or a user’s authorized representative, which has been agreed upon as a regular part of service delivery. Failure or degradation of service is handled as an incident.

The activities associated with matching skill or resource demands with the available skills or resources. The purpose of this process is to determine which skill or resource requirements (the demand) can be met using existing resources, determine which skill or resource requirements are not supported by currently available skills or resources (the gap) and determine the skills or resources for which no demand exists (excess). Resource and service component assignment happens both at the front office, where the customer contact occurs, and back-office, which is hidden from the customer and is often operated as a factory for efficiency.
The activities associated with the performance of tasks or actions which provide value to a customer.

The activities associated with comparing the differences between customers' expectations of a service and the perceptions of that service as it is delivered across various dimensions, including reliability, responsiveness, assurance, empathy, and tangibles.

The activities associated with receiving acknowledgment from the customer, or their authorized representative, that the services were rendered as specified in the Service Order and that the customer accepts the terms and conditions of the agreement and the Service Order.
The processes associated with keeping or restoring an asset to its working condition.

The activities associated with receiving and verifying the returned MRO item against the return authorization and other documentation and preparing the item for transfer. This process also applies to items that are being returned for retesting or upgrading.

The activities associated with the post-production documentation, testing, or certification required before delivering a finished product or service to the end customer. Examples include the assembly of batch records for regulatory agencies, laboratory tests for potency or purity, the creation of certificates of analysis or other quality records, and sign-off by the quality organization.

The activities associated with collecting and managing waste or surplus produced during the value-add and testing processes. Waste or surplus can include scrap material, unused resources, and non-conforming products or deliverables.

The process of scheduling, maintaining and dispositioning of MRO transformation assets developed for supply chain execution. This includes installation, repair, alteration, calibration and other activities necessary to sustain supply chain execution.

process_element_name: Diagnose the Conditions and Determine Disposition
process_element_definition: The activities associated with determining whether or not to repair, maintain or overhaul the item, what repair, maintenance, or overhaul is required, and who the appropriate MRO service provider would be to repair, maintain or overhaul the item. Possible outputs include decisions to send a return authorization request to the service provider, send the product back into service without returning or repairing it, or discard the item. This process also applies to items that are being returned for retesting or upgrading.

process_element_name: Open Request for Maintenance, Repair, or Overhaul
process_element_definition: The process of a customer requesting and obtaining authorization from an MRO service provider for the return of a maintenance, repair, and overhaul product. In addition to discussing the maintenance, repair, and overhaul issue, the customer and MRO service provider should discuss enabling conditions such as return replacement or credit, packaging, handling, transportation, and import and export requirements to facilitate the efficient return of the maintenance, repair, and overhaul product to the MRO service provider. This process also applies to items that are being returned for retesting or upgrading.

The activities associated with collecting and identifying the skills and resources currently available in the supply chain. Generally, this information is collected and organized by entity, such as supply chain node, department, function, or a combination of these. Examples of this process include data collection for standard headcount reports. Headcounts should include temporary staff and outsourced resources.
The activities associated with a customer developing the schedule for a carrier to pick up the MRO product and deliver it to the MRO service provider.

process_element_name: Issue Raw Material or Components or Subassemblies
process_element_definition: The process associated with the selection and physical movement of sourced or in-process products, including raw materials, fabricated components, subassemblies, required ingredients, and intermediate formulations or services, from a stocking or resource location to a specific point-of-use location. Issuing a product or resource includes the corresponding system transactions. The bill of materials or bill of service, routing information, and recipe or production instructions will determine the products to be issued to support the production operation(s).

The activities associated with retaining or restoring an item in or to a state in which it can perform its required function. The actions include combining all technical and corresponding administrative, managerial, and supervision actions.

The activities associated with inspection. These activities include examination and testing. Examination can be visual or dimensional, relying on the human senses or using simple methods of measurement and handling. Testing includes techniques by which functional, measurable characteristics, operability, supportability, or performance capability are quantitatively verified when subjected to controlled conditions that are real or simulated. Inspection is generally non-destructive and typically includes sight, hearing, smell, touch, taste, simple physical manipulation, mechanical and electrical gauging, and measurement. Testing often uses special test equipment or instrumentation to obtain accurate quantitative data to be analyzed.

The activities that containerize completed products for storage or sale to end users. Within certain industries, package activities may include cleaning or sterilization. Package activities do not apply to services.
